idea: ADD a LAN-based, known-devices-only remote-session connectivity transport ALONGSIDE Microsoft Dev Tunnels (Dev Tunnels stays default; LAN is opt-in/selectable). Motivation: the operator's corporate policy blocks Dev Tunnels, making the remote-session feature unusable. Primary target: Android e-ink tablet.

candidateDirections.name: Additive opt-in LAN listener gated by a NEW fail-closed server-side per-device cryptographic auth mode
candidateDirections.summary: New happy-server auth:'lan' mode + a LanDaemonProvider on the existing DaemonTunnelProvider seam + a codex Feature gate (default off); the known-devices allowlist is enforced cryptographically per-request at the listener (signed-request reusing Ed25519/X25519 TOFU keys, or mTLS), covering /pair/complete, all tunnel routes and the Socket.IO handshake, fail-closed, before any non-loopback bind. Dev Tunnels stays the unchanged default.

candidateDirections.name: Challenge the premise: reuse a policy-permitted outbound tunnel the operator already runs (Cloudflare provider-swap)
candidateDirections.summary: The operator already runs happy.evyatar.dev (a Cloudflare Tunnel). cloudflared is outbound-only (no LAN bind), so a CloudflareTunnelDaemonProvider preserves the entire gateway-as-identity-gate security model with ZERO teardown and could make the LAN effort unnecessary. Conflicts with the operator's 'no cloud' motivation; resolve with one operator question first.

candidateDirections.name: External cryptographic mesh (raw WireGuard) as the known-device boundary
candidateDirections.summary: Device identity = a pinned WireGuard public key enforced by the kernel before packets reach the loopback-bound listener, preserving the existing auth model with no new server mode. Dominant risk (all 3 lenses): the corp policy that blocks Dev Tunnels likely also blocks Tailscale coordination/DERP and may block UDP/client-isolated Wi-Fi, making it DOA; raw WG avoids the cloud but is heavy on e-ink.

questionsForSynthesis: PREMISE GATE (cheapest, do first): does the tablet currently reach happy.evyatar.dev (the operator's existing Cloudflare Tunnel) over the corporate network, and is 'no cloud at all' a hard requirement? If the tunnel works and cloud is acceptable, D-002 is far cheaper and the LAN effort may be unnecessary.

PHYSICAL-REACHABILITY PROBE: is the corp Wi-Fi AP/client-isolated or does it filter inbound LAN ports? If LAN peers can't see each other, every same-network transport is a NO-GO regardless of auth design.

Enforcement mechanism for D-001: per-device public-key signed-request (reuse Ed25519/X25519 TOFU material) vs mTLS client certs vs HMAC+nonce — which best balances airtight-ness vs React-Native/BOOX feasibility?
Concurrency: a THIRD listener alongside the live Dev Tunnels listener, or a user-selected single remote listener (Dev Tunnels default, LAN opt-in per daemon start)?

Discovery on e-ink: QR/manual LAN URL (reachability only) first with mDNS as non-security convenience later; how is DHCP IP churn / re-pinning handled, and where does the operator revoke known LAN devices?
Does relaxing the fork's own 'never expose on 0.0.0.0/LAN/tunnels' invariant (packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md Codex Transport Security Model) require a formal sign-off + docs/security-model.md update?
